mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic activity across manufacturing and construction sectors, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO increase by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and increasing for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher discount rates reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer spending, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profits, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises above 5.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and stable or declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a healthy economy supported by accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% and FEDFUNDS does not increase by more than 0.1% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 annualized growth > 3% and UNRATE < 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in the risk of an economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.
